title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (Early and Late Shows) on 1970-01-02
lineage: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC> SHN with aud patch

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of an early‑1970 Fillmore East show highlighted by a monster Dark Star → St Stephen → Eleven → Lovelight stretch and brilliant Mason’s Children, with only occasional vocal level glitches.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its adventurous Dark Star that rolls into a tight Eleven and a crowd‑loving Lovelight, plus standout moments from Mason’s Children, Casey Jones, Hard to Handle and High Time.  The soundboard source is generally clear and vivid, though a few reviewers note low vocal levels, channel swaps and missing edit points that require a bit of patience.  Overall the show feels like a pivotal early‑70 set that rewards repeated listening.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (30+) award 4–5 stars and celebrate the musical peaks, while the few technical complaints keep the rating from the top tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑balanced; some listeners note vocals unusually low, occasional channel swaps, speed waver corrections needed on a few tracks, and missing edit points (e.g., Dark Star → St Stephen cut).

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Zarathustra intro leads into a funky first set; the second half builds to an epic Dark Star → St Stephen → Eleven → Lovelight sequence that defines the show’s momentum, despite a few patched sections.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar work receives repeated praise – “perfect tone”, “on this night”, “jams that knock Little Dave in the dirt” and even humorous moments like his chuckle during Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is highlighted as a “big fat bass line” that anchors the Lovelight groove.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ on Cosmic Charlie and early songs gets strong kudos; Pigpen’s keyboard contributions are also noted as “on fire”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey receive acclaim for tight, powerful drumming – “tight 11”, “drum runs perfect”, and “Mickey's cannon”.
